extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, publishers, and others interested in peer review innovation and patient partnership in research publishing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and practical standards for inviting, recruiting, supporting, and using patients and caregivers as manuscript reviewers alongside traditional peer reviewers in a medical journal editorial process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: when to include patient review
rubrics_metrics.description: Invite patient reviewers for most research papers, particularly those where patients were recruited into the study reported; recognise that it is not appropriate for all papers (for example, we don’t routinely invite patients and carers to review methodological research papers or journalology papers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patient review has been extended beyond research papers to educational articles and some comment articles. Editors should apply judgement about appropriateness on a per-manuscript basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient reviewer qualifications / eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Welcome all patients and carers to review; there are no pre-conditions for joining the database. The journal is interested in their lived experience of illness, medical interventions, and treatments, and any advocacy work they undertake for fellow patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not require formal methodological or statistical expertise; reviewers should be free to decline invitations. The emphasis is on lived experience rather than formal credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment and maintenance of patient reviewer database
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruit via a patient partnership panel, patient editors, outreach to specific patient groups and organisations, and by embedding invitations to readers to recommend patients; allow organic growth as patient reviewers share within their networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a registration form and visible guidance for prospective patient reviewers; use patient editors and panels as constant sources of outreach and advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and focus of patient reviewers' comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Patient reviewers are not asked to critically appraise/comment on the validity of the studies reported but they are very welcome to do so. Their contributions focus on insight into what it’s like to experience a condition, relevance of outcomes, clarity, and practical implications for patients and carers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should take patient comments into account alongside peer reviewers’ comments at internal decision meetings. Encourage patient reviewers to stick to issues they feel important even if they lack methodological expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and process for invitations and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Invite patient reviewers at the same time as peer reviewers and ask both groups to submit their reviews within 14 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed not to increase review times — BMJ reports the average interval between invitation and submission for patient review is slightly faster than standard peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of competing interests and anonymity policy
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviewers, including patient reviewers, are asked to declare any competing interests. The BMJ has an open peer review policy where reviewers’ identities are stated in the review, but a few patients (and peer reviewers) have asked to review anonymously and those requests have been accommodated on a case-by-case basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform all reviewers that reviews will be published online and make clear the options and trade-offs regarding anonymity vs open review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of reviews (open peer review / pre-publication history)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish the full pre-publication history for research papers online, including reviewers’ comments and reviewers’ identities (subject to accepted anonymity requests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most patient reviewers support open review; nonetheless, provide the option to anonymise in exceptional cases and explain the journal’s policy up front.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory author declarations of patient and public involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Require authors of research papers to document if and how they involved patients in their study as a mandatory requirement, with set questions including involvement in defining the research question and outcome measures, design and implementation of the study, and dissemination of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the declaration part of submission requirements to increase transparency and facilitate assessment of patient involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of patient reviews into editorial decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Take patient reviewers’ comments into account along with peer reviewers’ comments during internal editorial meetings where decisions about publication or rejection are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should weigh patient input alongside scientific criteria (originality, scientific robustness, relevance). Expect decisions to remain based on multiple factors; BMJ does not anticipate major changes to acceptance rates solely from patient review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support, guidance, and feedback for patient reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear guidance on what is being asked of patient reviewers and clarify why it is important; elicit early and continuing feedback from reviewers, authors, and editors to inform the process. Reviewers value brief feedback on reviews to help improve confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer tangible recognition (e.g., a year’s subscription, annual recognition on the website, awards such as Best Patient Reviewer), invite reviewers into other journal activities (judging panels, writing opportunities), and offer training or examples where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring, evaluation and basic metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Track operational metrics and run surveys: BMJ reports ~700 registered patient reviewers, ~2,000 invitations sent, 754 completed patient reviews, and similar acceptance/return rates to peer reviewers; a survey of recent patient reviewers had a 74% response rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quantitative tracking and qualitative surveys to evaluate engagement, quality of comments, how authors respond to patient input, and consider formal evaluations (e.g., studying author responses or any effect on acceptance rates) as follow-up research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author and community acceptance considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors have responded courteously and constructively to patient reviewer points when revising papers; patient reviewers have reported feeling valued and included rather than tokenised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate clearly with authors about the role of patient reviewers and gather feedback; consider phasing and outreach so journals adopting the practice are not 'left behind' and can learn from early adopters.
